strengths: Addresses a practical problem in online 3D reconstruction with a training-free, plug-and-play solution that maintains efficiency (20 FPS, 6GB memory)
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple tasks (pose estimation, depth, 3D reconstruction) and datasets with clear improvements on long sequences (~2× better ATE)
Well-presented with clear motivation and effective visualizations; novel perspective of reinterpreting RNN-based 3D reconstruction through Test-Time Training lens
Strong empirical results on long-sequence scenarios with clear qualitative improvements showing better handling of forgetting and loop closure
Solid experimental design with both short and long-sequence evaluations, detailed metrics, and reproducibility details
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: the core contribution (confidence-guided learning rate via Eq. 7) is relatively simple—essentially summing attention scores and applying sigmoid—with intuitive but shallow motivation

Incomplete solution: paper acknowledges method 'mitigates but does not resolve state forgetting'; significant accuracy gaps remain with offline methods (e.g., VGGT), limiting the contribution's impact

Loose theoretical justification: the connection between cross-attention (Eq. 3) and TTT gradient updates (Eq. 4) is suggestive rather than rigorous; softmax normalization differs fundamentally from gradient descent, yet the reformulation in Eq. 6-8 lacks mathematical rigor
Critical missing ablations: no ablation studies validating design choices (why sum spatial dimension? why sigmoid? alternative confidence metrics?); Figure 5 provides only qualitative intuition

Narrow scope of applicability: method is specifically engineered for CUT3R's architecture; unclear generalization to other RNNs or online reconstruction approaches, making contributions somewhat application-specific

Short-sequence competitive performance unclear: Table 1 shows TTT3R competitive but not clearly superior to baseline on short sequences (50-110 frames); main gains on very long sequences (hundreds-thousands frames) whose practical necessity is unclear
Missing key comparisons: Long3R (Ref. 18), a concurrent streaming reconstruction method, is cited but not compared; incomplete coverage of recent related work

strengths: Clear problem formulation addressing a practical limitation of RNN-based 3D reconstruction methods
Novel TTT perspective that provides a principled framework for analyzing state update mechanisms in 3D reconstruction
Comprehensive experimental validation across three tasks and six datasets with thorough ablation studies
Strong long-sequence performance with ~2× improvement in pose estimation accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency
Training-free, plug-and-play solution with practical utility and promised code release
Honest discussion of limitations and transparent presentation of state reset workaround
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies existing TTT concepts to CUT3R rather than developing fundamentally new methods; per-token confidence-based learning rates have been explored (Gated Linear Attention, concurrent confidence-filtering work)
Incomplete solution to stated problem: method fails beyond ~1000 frames requiring ad-hoc state reset mechanism (Appendix B) with additional hyperparameters

Weak theoretical justification for the specific closed-form learning rate β_t in Eq. 7: why averaging cross-attention over spatial dimensions is optimal is not rigorously derived; deviates from standard TTT without clear motivation

Questionable experimental comparisons: learnable gating baselines dismissed as 'prohibitively costly' to train on longer sequences without supporting cost analysis; short sequence results show TTT3R is competitive but not clearly superior to all baselines
Limited scope: method applied only to CUT3R with no exploration of generalizability to other RNN architectures, undermining claims of introducing a 'general TTT-based framework'
State reset mechanism is underemphasized despite being necessary for practical long-sequence use (>1000 frames), and its dependence on 'global metric camera poses' raises reproducibility questions
Missing ablations on activation function choice and alternative confidence aggregation strategies; Figure 5 provides only qualitative analysis of β_t behavior
Presentation issues: inconsistent notation (Σ_m as both sum and mean), critical architectural details relegated to appendix, overclaiming in title/abstract relative to actual scope
